one_liner: A George Mason University staff role coaching students in the ACCESS Academy program on careers and building partnerships with employers and industry.
fit_summary: Daniel's outgoing, relationship-building style and comfort with the public match the coaching and liaison halves of this title. Experience at IEM working with government clients can be framed as stakeholder and partner engagement. No description is available, so the fit depends on duties, and possibly education or coaching credentials, that are not yet known.
eligibility: Confirm on the full posting at jobs.virginia.gov or jobs.gmu.edu whether a bachelor's degree or career-services experience is required; none is stated here.
GMU positions are Virginia state employment, so prior federal status is not needed and veterans' preference generally does not apply.
Check whether the role is classified, a wage position, or grant-funded or restricted (ACCESS Academy may be a funded program), because this affects benefits and duration.
Location is the Fairfax campus with no remote option listed; the commute from Manassas is manageable.
strategy: Open the full posting before applying; this brief rests only on the title, so align your resume to the actual duties and qualifications listed there.
Frame your IEM work around client and partner relationships: coordinating with government agencies, explaining complex programs to non-experts, and supporting preparedness or recovery teams.
Emphasize people skills with concrete examples, such as presenting, training, mentoring, or event and outreach work, that show you can coach students and pitch partnerships to employers.
Use your public-policy knowledge as a selling point for connecting students to government and public-sector careers, a strong employer pipeline in Northern Virginia.
Apply soon even though the posting is open until filled, and include a short cover letter tying your interest in workforce development to GMU's mission.
State schools do not impose the federal two-page cap, but keep your resume to about two pages and tailored to this role.
resume_bullets: Built and maintained working relationships with [number/type] government client stakeholders at IEM, coordinating [meetings/deliverables] on [emergency management/recovery project].
Presented [topic] to [audience size/type], translating complex policy and program requirements into clear, actionable guidance.
Coordinated [outreach/training/event] involving [number] partners, resulting in [outcome you can verify].
interview_questions: How would you build relationships with new industry partners who have never worked with the program?
Describe a time you coached or guided someone toward a goal; what was your approach?
How would you help a student who is unsure of their career direction?
How does your consulting experience prepare you for a university liaison role?
watch_outs: No job description, salary, or qualifications are available, so verify all of them before investing heavily in the application.
The role may be grant-funded or restricted, which could limit its duration; ask about funding during the interview.
If a degree or prior career-services experience is required, confirm you meet it.
